Share on X Telegram The Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) has demanded justice for its staff member, Mr Oscar Eze, who was stabbed to death in Umunede, Delta State, over an electricity disconnection. Already, five suspects have been arrested, while others are still at large, even as the commission insists on pursuing the case. The Acting Managing Director of BEDC, Mr Jonathan Lawani, disclosed this on Wednesday during a news briefing at the company’s headquarters in Benin. Lawani said Eze, 38, was killed on Monday, November 16, while carrying out an official assignment in the community. He said the deceased had disconnected a property over an outstanding electricity bill of nearly N300,000, after which some persons traced him to a house in the community and stabbed him repeatedly, leaving him dead at the scene. He explained that the disconnection was carried out in line with the regulatory framework governing electricity distribution. “The only instrument that NERC has approved to demand payment from those who refuse to pay their monthly electricity bills is disconnection,” he said. Lawani condemned the killing, stressing that electricity workers should not be attacked for performing their official duties. “The fact that we come to your house to demand payment for the service we have rendered, irrespective of your dissatisfaction with our service, does not give you the right to attack,” he said. He disclosed that the company’s management visited the Assistant Inspector-General of Police’s office, the Divisional Police Officer in Umunede and the scene of the incident on Tuesday. He added that five suspects had been arrested, while others were still at large. The acting managing director said the deceased left behind a son from an earlier marriage, a wife he married four months ago and an elderly mother. He called on the Delta State government to provide adequate security for electricity workers, warning that continued attacks could threaten BEDC’s operations in the state. “We believe that the government should provide an enabling environment for people to work, and for a critical sector like electricity, we should be protected,” he said. Lawani said the company would pursue the case until justice was served. “We cannot recover his life. We can never take his life back to his people. But one thing is that we must bring justice to him,” he said. Lawani advised customers dissatisfied with BEDC’s services to use the company’s complaint channels or approach the relevant electricity regulatory authorities for redress. He urged electricity consumers to resolve disputes through established channels rather than resort to violence against workers. Also speaking, Dr Abel Enechaziam, Head of Maximum Demand Customer and Acting Chief Commercial Officer of BEDC, called on state governments to protect electricity workers across the states where the company operates. Enechaziam said the company could no longer tolerate attacks and harassment of personnel providing electricity services. “We cannot continue to tolerate this kind of event. It is very sad,” he said. He urged the public to stop molesting and harassing service providers in the electricity sector.
